description: The fused megakernel (mega_eigh n<=200, mega_eigh_med 200<n<=448) is now the HOT kernel on FIVE benchmark shapes: direct solver for shapes 1 (n176 b40) & 2 (n352 b40), AND -- via brief-11's inner-solve routing -- the k-block eigh for shapes 3 (dense512 k352), 8 (rankdef512 k384), 12 (lapgeom1024 k384). nsys on shape 3 shows mega_eigh_med_k is 48.9% of the shape (52ms); ncu shows it is BARRIER-BOUND: 47.6% barrier stalls, only 50% occupancy -- NOT compute-bound. Attack the kernel internals so a single speedup compounds across all 5 shapes: cut the __syncthreads count (warp-specialize the tred2 tridiagonalization / tql2 QL-iteration stages; use warp-shuffle reductions where a reduction fits within a warp; double-buffer the SMEM panel to overlap load with compute), RAISE occupancy (shrink the packed-FP16 SMEM footprint and/or register pressure so >1 CTA can be resident per SM, and/or retune NT/NB), and overlap the compact-WY back-transform with the solve. Keep the packed-FP16 lower-tri SMEM layout, the Sturm-bisection/twisted eigenvalue solve, and the residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback. -O2 not -O3. Forks best 12251fe so the kernel speedup stacks on the inner-solve routing. Distinct from brief-12 (a NEW QL kernel for n=32, occupancy-bound by batch=20) -- this optimizes the EXISTING n=176-448 megakernel's internal barriers.

Switch megakernel build -O3 --use_fast_math -> -O2 (run's mandated hard constraint: O3+fastmath reorder SMEM across __syncthreads -> nondeterministic at large batch). Cost of the switch: geomean 41456->42235us (+1.9%); all 5 megakernel-hot shapes slower (shape1 n176 2533->2810, shape2 n352 10874->11645, shape3 dense512 109881->113820, shape8 rankdef512 121184->125368, shape12 lapgeom1024 46461->47413). 39/39 validate. This is the correctness-mandated baseline the kernel-internal barrier/occupancy work must beat.

Warp-shuffle two-level block reductions (both megakernels): replace per-level tree reduction (~10 barriers each) with intra-warp __shfl_down_sync (0 barriers) + one cross-warp pass through red[] (2 barriers). All 5 reduction sites per kernel (amax, s2, vp, glo/ghi). geomean 42235->41950us (-0.7% vs t1 -O2 baseline). shape1 2810->2748, shape2 11645->11247, shape3 113820->111750, shape8 125368->123121, shape12 47413->46952. 39/39 validate. Modest -- structural symv/rank-2 barriers per iter remain the bigger lever.

Fuse v-init loop + vp-into-symv (both megakernels), -2 barriers/iter in stage-1 tridiag loop (~9->7). (1) v[i] and Rm column set in one loop (drops zero-init barrier); (2) vp=v.p accumulated inside symv on own p[i] (drops symv->vp barrier). geomean 41950->41742us (-0.5% vs t2). shape1 2748->2736, shape2 11247->11075, shape3 111750->110773, shape8 123121->122315, shape12 46952->46648. 39/39 validate. Cumulative from -O2 baseline: -1.2%.

Single-barrier reductions (write nw warp partials, 1 barrier, every thread re-reduces redundantly) + fused _blkRedMinMax. REGRESSED hot shapes: geomean 41742->41920us (+0.4%). shape2 11075->11251, shape3 110773->111756, shape8 122315->123468, shape12 46648->46906; only small n176 improved (2736->2715, nw=8 cheap). At NT=1024/nw=32 the 32-wide redundant re-reduce + lost 2nd barrier costs more than the saved barrier. 39/39 validate. Reverting to two-barrier form next.

Revert t4 single-barrier reductions to two-barrier form (t4 regressed hot shapes); keep fused _blkRedMinMax (min+max in one two-barrier pass, saves the Sturm between-reduction barrier). geomean 41800us -- ties t3 (41742) within noise. shape2 11059, shape3 110769, shape8 122289, shape12 46577. 39/39 validate. Two-barrier reductions + t3 fusions are the stable base.

Reflector store Rm -> column-major (Rm[c*n+i]) so per-column spill writes are coalesced (ncu flagged 33% excessive global sectors); re-indexed back-transform Y-load to keep its reads coalesced. NEUTRAL: geomean 41775us vs t5 41800 (within noise). shape2 11125, shape3 111102, shape8 122571, shape12 46775. 39/39 validate. Confirms kernel is barrier/latency-bound at 1 CTA/SM, not memory-coalescing-bound -- ncu per-metric estimates aren't additive when barriers gate. Lever is barrier count / occupancy (SMEM hard-caps 1 CTA for n>=333).

Small-kernel NT sweep 256/512/1024: shape1 n176 = 2731 (256) < 2741 (512) < 2783 (1024); kept 256. Small kernel not occupancy-starved at n176 b40 (SMEM caps 1 CTA/SM; only 40 CTAs on 148 SMs). geomean 41848us (ties t5/t6 within noise). 39/39 validate. NT is a non-lever.

Fold w=p-K*v into rank-2 inner loop (drops the O(n) p-=K*v loop + 1 barrier, 6 barriers/col) but recomputes p[j]-K*v[j] for every (i,j) O(n^2). NEUTRAL: geomean 41806us vs t7 41848 (noise). Small kernel improved (shape1 2741->2719), med hot shapes slightly worse (shape2 11148->11299, shape3 111157->112018). Added O(n^2) inner work offsets saved O(n) loop+barrier. 39/39 validate. Barrier-reduction plateau confirmed. Best remains t3 (41742).

CONSOLIDATED BEST: union of every helpful kernel-internal change, minus t8's O(n^2) inner-fold. Both megakernels carry: warp-shuffle two-level block reductions (t2), unified v/Rm build + vp-fused-into-symv (t3, -2 barriers/col), fused _blkRedMinMax Sturm bound (t5, -1 barrier), column-major Rm[c*n+i] coalesced spill (t6), precompute w=p-K*v once (beats t8), small-kernel NT=256 (t7 sweep). STABLE across 3 re-benchmarks: 41828/41822/41842us (0.05% spread). vs -O2 mandated baseline (t1 42235): -1.0%. shape1 n176 2735, shape2 n352 11140, shape3 dense512 111212, shape8 rankdef512 122557, shape12 lapgeom1024 46763. 39/39 validate. ncu: barrier stalls STILL 48.8%, occupancy STILL 50% (SMEM+regs both cap 1 CTA/SM) -- barrier COUNT cuts reduced total instructions (~1% wall) but not the stall FRACTION (each remaining barrier still stalls 32 warps ~8.8cyc with no other resident block). The -O2 tax (~1.9%) can't fully close: kernel is latency-bound at hard-capped 50% occupancy.

Worked the megakernel-internal barrier/occupancy brief across 9 trials. BEST = t9 (b6bf2065), geomean 41828us, STABLE across 3 re-benchmarks (41828/41822/41842, 0.05% spread), 39/39 validate. Parent 12251fe was 41456us BUT compiled with -O3 --use_fast_math which the run's HARD constraint BANS (they reorder SMEM across __syncthreads -> nondeterministic at large batch). t1 switched to the mandated -O2 = 42235us (+1.9% tax, the real correctness baseline). The kernel-internal work recovered ~1.0% of that tax (42235->41828); net vs the banned -O3 parent is +0.9%.

WHAT MOVED THE NEEDLE (all on both mega_eigh + mega_eigh_med, both stage-1 hot loop): warp-shuffle two-level block reductions replacing the ~10-barrier tree (t2, -0.7%); unified v/Rm-column build loop + vp-fused-into-symv dropping 2 barriers/col (t3, -0.5%, the single best trial 41742); fused min+max Sturm-bound reduction (t5); column-major reflector store Rm[c*n+i] for coalesced spills (t6, neutral). Cumulative stage-1 barrier count ~9->6 per column.

WHAT DIDN'T (measured, refuted): (a) single-barrier redundant-re-reduce REGRESSED at NT=1024 (t4 41920, the 32-wide re-reduce costs more than the saved barrier); (b) folding w=p-K*v into the O(n^2) rank-2 inner loop NEUTRAL-to-worse (t8, extra FMAs offset the saved O(n) loop+barrier); (c) small-kernel NT sweep 256/512/1024 -> 256 already best (shape1 not occupancy-starved); (d) Rm coalescing NEUTRAL on wall-clock -> kernel is NOT memory-coalescing-bound.

ROOT CAUSE (ncu --set full on mega_eigh_med_k shape3, final t9): barrier stalls STILL 48.8%, occupancy STILL 50%, UNCHANGED from parent despite cutting ~3 barriers/col. Block Limit Shared Mem=1 AND Block Limit Registers=1 (127KB packed-FP16 SMEM + 64 regs/thread both cap 1 CTA/SM). At 1 CTA/SM the barrier STALL FRACTION is structural: each remaining __syncthreads stalls all 32 warps ~8.8cyc with NO other resident block to hide behind, so cutting barrier COUNT lowers total instructions (~1% wall) but not the stall fraction. The two occupancy limiters CANNOT both be lifted at n>=333: packed-FP16 lower-tri is already the minimal SMEM footprint (124KB at n=352, 148KB at n=384) so >1 CTA/SM is impossible; NT=1024 already maxes warps/CTA at 32 = the 50% ceiling.

OPEN DIRECTIONS the manager may pursue (I did NOT reach/close these): (1) BREAK THE 1-CTA/SM SMEM CAP -- the only path to >50% occupancy. Store the trailing submatrix in packed-FP16 but SHRINK the resident footprint as the reduction advances (columns [0,c) are done), or tile the matrix so 2 half-CTAs cooperate per matrix -- both are large rewrites and risk the fused stage-handoff. (2) BREAK THE SERIAL PER-COLUMN DEPENDENCY -- a blocked/panel latrd would batch the trailing rank-2 update but I reasoned (did not build) that it ADDS per-column panel-projection barriers and its classic cache-reuse benefit is moot for an already-SMEM-resident kernel; a two-stage dense->band->tridiag (band width b, b columns reduced per panel with ONE trailing GEMM) is the real barrier-count reducer but overlaps briefs 1/3/4/6 dense-reduction territory. (3) OVERLAP back-transform with solve (brief's 3rd lever, untried) -- stage 4 compact-WY has ~900 barriers at n=352; interleaving its column-blocks with the twisted-eigenvector stage-3 (which is barrier-free per-ev) could hide them, but the data dependency (back-transform needs the eigenvectors) makes true overlap hard. (4) RECLAIM THE -O2 TAX SAFELY -- probe selective -O3 on ONLY the reduction-free stages (Sturm/twisted, which have no cross-__syncthreads SMEM reorder risk) via separate TUs while keeping -O2 on stage-1/4; could recover ~1% without the nondeterminism. (5) LOWER-PRECISION SYMV -- the symv/rank-2 (LSU-bound 41.9%, the O(n^2)/col dominant work) reads packed FP16 already; a tensor-core (tcgen05 on sm_100a) batched symv across the trailing panel could cut the SIMT bottleneck but needs the panel structure of (2). None of these is refuted -- all are unbuilt; (1) and (3) are the highest-ceiling for THIS kernel, (4) is the cheapest ~1% recovery.
